newsitem.title: UK: Sega Europe expects growth in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Sega Europe expects growth in 1997.

text.p: Sega Europe, part of Japan's Sega Enterprises Ltd, said on Tuesday it expected increased sales levels this year for its videogames business on both the Saturn and PC platforms.

"We expect to show increased growth in 1997 in all our key business areas," Sega Europe chief executive Malcolm Miller said in a statement. "We are on track to reach our sales target of a million Sega Saturn games consoles across Europe by the spring."

"Our PC games business continues to grow well, with sales particularly buoyant in the key European markets of the UK and Germany. Anticipating a Christmas surge in sales of Pentium-based PCs, we have been holding our best titles for release in the first quarter," he added.

Sega Europe said its 16-bit business continued to do well, despite the recent announcement by its parent company that it would be writing off inventories of Mega CD and 32X peripherals in America and Japan.
